result.topic_en: Solving the linear congruence $ax+b\equiv c$ when the modulus is prime to $a$, by reducing it to $ax\equiv\pm1$, i.e. to the indeterminate equation $ax=by\pm1$, and introducing a bracket notation for the continued-fraction (continuant) algorithm.

methods.what: Reduction of the linear congruence $ax+b\equiv c$ to $ax\equiv\pm1$: if $x\equiv r$ solves the latter, then $x\equiv\pm r(c-b)$ solves the former
methods.quote:
$ax\equiv\pm 1$ pendere ; cui si satisfacit
$x\equiv r$, propositae satisfaciet
$x\equiv\pm r(c-b)$

methods.what: Equivalence of the congruence $ax\equiv\pm1 \pmod b$ with the indeterminate (linear Diophantine) equation $ax=by\pm1$
methods.quote:
$ax$ [-$\equiv r(c-b)$-] $\equiv\pm 1$ (Mod. b) cui aequivalet aequatio
indeterminata $ax=by\pm 1$
